title: First photo of Earth from space
body:
This grainy picture was taken from a Nazi weapon, over New Mexico, and it is the first photo of Earth from space.

24 October 1946. At White Sands, scientists launched a captured German V-2 rocket with a 35mm movie camera bolted into its nose. The rocket climbed about 65 miles, far higher than any airplane or balloon, and filmed the Earth below as it rose.

Then it fell back, hitting the desert at roughly 500 feet per second. The rocket was wrecked. But the film had been sealed inside a steel case.

A recovery team drove out into the desert to find it, including 19 year old Fred Rulli. The film was intact. When the footage was first shown, he later recalled, the scientists were overjoyed.

The rockets built to bomb London had given humanity its first look back at home.
photoNote: The actual frame from the V-2 camera. U.S. Army, White Sands, public domain. Grainy by nature, which suits the card.
